PHL.note: FAOSTAT 2023 production ~5.9 Mt; exports ~1.2 Mt mainly to Japan, China, Korea (Panama-disease pressure cut volumes).

CRI.note: FAOSTAT 2023 production ~2.4 Mt; Costa Rica is a top-3 exporter (~2.0 Mt) led by Del Monte, Dole, Chiquita.

COL.note: FAOSTAT 2023 production ~2.4 Mt; Colombia exports ~2.0 Mt (Uraba, Magdalena).

GTM.note: FAOSTAT 2023 production ~4.6 Mt; Guatemala is the leading supplier to the US (~2.7 Mt exports).

DOM.note: FAOSTAT 2023 production ~0.9 Mt; Dominican Republic is the world's largest organic/fair-trade banana exporter (~0.4 Mt).

HND.note: FAOSTAT 2023 production ~0.75 Mt; Honduras exports ~0.47 Mt, almost entirely to the US.

CIV.note: FAOSTAT 2023 production ~0.45 Mt; Cote d'Ivoire is the leading African banana exporter to the EU (~0.33 Mt).

CMR.note: FAOSTAT 2023 production ~1.3 Mt; Cameroon exports ~0.38 Mt to the EU (PHP/Compagnie Fruitiere).

PAN.note: FAOSTAT 2023 production ~0.5 Mt; Panama exports ~0.4 Mt to EU and US.

PER.note: FAOSTAT 2023 production ~0.25 Mt; Peru is a leading organic banana exporter (~0.2 Mt).

MEX.note: FAOSTAT 2023 production ~2.5 Mt; Mexico exports ~0.56 Mt to the US, Japan.

USA.note: UN Comtrade 2024: the US imported 5,244 kt of bananas (HS 0803), the world's largest importer; negligible domestic output.

DEU.note: FAO 2023: Germany imports ~1.3 Mt bananas, much re-exported within the EU. Comtrade 2024 not in preview API; carried on FAO basis.

NLD.note: UN Comtrade 2024: Netherlands imported 1,162 kt (HS 0803); Rotterdam is a major EU gateway with large onward re-exports.

RUS.note: FAO/USDA 2023-24: Russia imports ~1.45 Mt bananas, overwhelmingly from Ecuador. Comtrade 2024 not in preview API; FAO basis.

JPN.note: UN Comtrade 2024: Japan imported 1,042 kt (HS 0803), led by the Philippines (~790 kt) and Ecuador.

CHN.note: FAOSTAT 2023 production ~12 Mt (Yunnan, Hainan, Guangxi); China imports ~1.8 Mt, mainly from the Philippines and SE Asia.

GBR.note: FAO 2023: UK imports ~1.0 Mt bananas, led by Colombia, Dominican Republic, Ecuador. Comtrade 2024 line basis mixed; FAO basis.

IND.note: FAOSTAT 2023: India is the world's largest banana producer (~35 Mt) but almost all is consumed domestically; minor Gulf exports.

companies.name: Chiquita
companies.note: One of the 'big three' banana marketers; sources from owned and contracted farms across Central America and Colombia, shipping to North America and Europe.
companies.improve: Should disclose farm-level water-use and Panama-disease (TR4) containment data.

companies.name: Dole
companies.note: World's largest fresh-produce company after the 2021 Total Produce/Dole merger; major banana grower-shipper in Latin America and the Philippines.
companies.improve: Should publish origin-level deforestation and living-wage audit results.

companies.name: Fresh Del Monte Produce
companies.note: Third of the 'big three'; vertically integrated with owned plantations, ships and ripening centres serving the US, EU, Middle East, Asia.
companies.improve: Should expand TR4 biosecurity reporting and Scope-3 shipping emissions.

companies.name: Fyffes
companies.note: Leading EU banana importer (owned by Japan's Sumitomo since 2017); strong in fair-trade and the UK/Irish retail channel.
companies.improve: Should give greater transparency on grower pricing under Sumitomo ownership.

companies.name: Grupo Noboa (Bonita)
companies.note: Ecuador's flagship banana exporter under the Bonita brand; dominant in shipments to Russia, the Middle East and the Mediterranean.
companies.improve: Should commission independent labour-rights and pesticide-exposure auditing on contracted farms.

companies.name: Grupo Acon
companies.note: Major independent Costa Rican banana grower-exporter supplying the big marketers and EU retail.
companies.improve: Should publish water-stewardship and agrochemical-runoff metrics for the Caribbean lowlands.

global.note: Global bananas, kt. Production/consumption from FAOSTAT (HS 0803 incl. plantains). Export volumes from FAO/USDA; world banana trade ~20 Mt amid TR4 disease pressure and freight swings.
